--- docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
+++ docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
@@ -274,12 +274,14 @@
 
 Raw reports admit at most50,000 decisions and50,000 outcomes,6 policies including learning (the existing4 presets plus1 custom fit),800 raw ledger objects,16MiB per object and combined raw UTF-8 text,1,000,000 estimated work units,16,384 projected item/slot/ancestor cells across policies, and8MiB final report JSON. Work includes ring construction/sorting, policy/outcome filtering/sorting and featured-product cross-products; listing traversal is also bounded. Consumed components are limited to256 UTF-8 bytes and generated keys to2048 bytes; invalid shapes or inherited object-property names return400. Capacity refusal returns no-store413 with `code:report_budget_exceeded`, `budget`, `limit` and `observed`, before any partial raw publication; object refusals retain `objects`/`max`. General capped loader callers retain their separate truncation contract. Native object size and actual stream bytes are checked; text-only adapters can check actual bytes only after materialization. These are application safety budgets, not proved Worker CPU/memory, supported customer traffic or scientific policy limits.
 
-Aggregate-to-day construction separately admits at most24 distinct canonical hours,16MiB combined aggregate JSON,6 policy names,1,000,000 estimated merge/admission work units,16,384 projected cells and8MiB report JSON before publication. Saved day reads admit8MiB per object; windows admit16MiB combined input and16,384 consumed/pooled rows or cells. Day/window GET responses are capped at8MiB including their response envelope. Required owner/shape failures and unavailable storage return sanitized no-store503; only an actual absent object is missing. These guards preserve accepted counts and conservative legacy coverage without rewriting stored objects. Large legacy windows can refuse even below92 days. Hour-fold/shard ingestion, configuration/tombstone loads, grid paging, policy compatibility, model acceptance, full long-window measurement and native capacity remain separate work.
+Aggregate-to-day construction separately admits at most24 distinct canonical hours,16MiB combined aggregate JSON,6 policy names,1,000,000 estimated merge/admission work units,16,384 projected cells and8MiB report JSON before publication. Saved day reads admit8MiB per object; windows admit16MiB combined input and16,384 consumed/pooled rows or cells. Day/window GET responses are capped at8MiB including their response envelope. Required owner/shape failures and unavailable storage return sanitized no-store503; only an actual absent object is missing. These guards preserve accepted counts and conservative legacy coverage without rewriting stored objects. Large legacy windows can refuse even below92 days. Hour-fold/shard ingestion, configuration/tombstone loads, policy compatibility, model acceptance, full long-window measurement and native capacity remain separate work.
 
 New canonical raw/hourly publications store a leading reserved `_summary` version1 in the same JSON object and the same single put as all original report fields. The summary's first line ends with comma+LF and is limited to64KiB UTF-8 including framing; the complete canonical object remains limited to8MiB. Explicit custom/empty/preset arrays remain response-only and do not acquire this storage-summary limit. Public POST/day GET report shapes remain unchanged. Window reads request the first64KiB and validate only the summary, preserving raw arm counts and normalized coverage without parsing grids. All received bytes, including chunk tails, count toward the window budget. This does not verify unread grid/tail integrity. Legacy objects use a verified complete small read or a separate bounded full read as the sole version, charging prefix plus fallback bytes; a disappeared or corrupt fallback is unavailable, not missing. Older writers can restore the coherent but slower legacy format. There is no sidecar, dual-write consistency protocol, migration or history repair. Local range/byte evidence is not deployed Worker capacity, policy compatibility or scientific/customer acceptance.
 
-Custom report results remain usable in the POST response and the legacy UI's local CSV download, but reload GET/window reads the canonical saved report. This forward isolation does not detect or repair prior overwrites, certify old writers, resolve concurrent canonical publications or strengthen canonical write acknowledgements.
+Day GET optionally accepts `slot`, `limit` (1–500, default50) and an opaque `cursor`. It returns `{ok,report,page}`: grids contain only that slot's sorted cross-policy item page and pooled `'*'` cells/slot rates, while counts, policies and coverage describe the same saved report. Missing pooled evidence stays absent. `page` carries `slot,revision,total,offset,limit,next,previous`; cursors bind the full saved content SHA-256 and exact tenant/brand/date/slot/limit. Invalid or mismatched queries return400; changed content returns409 and requires a first-page reload. Paging parameters require a slot. Each page still reads and validates the bounded full saved object server-side; this is response/DOM containment, not storage-read or CPU/SLO improvement.
 
+Both comparison views use paged canonical GETs. Ordinary unpaged GET retains the full diagnostic shape; optional `revision=<64 lowercase hex>` requires that exact saved content or returns409. The legacy CSV action explicitly requests this full revision-matched report, including every policy/item/cell for the selected slot, never just the visible page. Custom POST results remain response-only: the legacy view retains the full custom result for local slot/page navigation and complete CSV, without canonical fetches replacing it. Date/brand/user changes clear that local context. Modern canonical builds reload the latest saved first page and distinguish it from the POST candidate: existing write acknowledgements do not prove those objects equal. Neither this forward isolation nor paging repairs historical overwrites, certifies old writers, resolves concurrent canonical publications or strengthens canonical write acknowledgements.
+
 W29 availability: stored `assisted`/`autonomous` configuration is retained but dormant; neither a stored mode nor an old client enables automation. The slots index's `autonomy` field describes stored configuration, and `learn/queue.proposals_pending` counts historical `proposed` statuses, not actionable work. Both consoles withdraw autonomy editing and proposal decisions. Safe autonomy remains an unmet delivery obligation, not a waived requirement.
 
 ## 6. Operators: sign-in and accounts
